prompts.prompt: Our threat-modeling reviewers need an AWS architecture diagram of the receipts service before Thursday's security review. Turn system-design.md into a draw.io diagram they can import into draw.io and our Design Inspector tool. Write it as uncompressed mxGraphModel XML to diagrams/receipts.drawio, and include every service the doc mentions, including the operations pieces. Reviewers will use it to reason about trust boundaries and data flows, so make those readable. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in a text note inside the diagram, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill prescribes scope placement (global services like S3/CloudFront/WAF inside the account but outside the VPC, regional services outside the VPC, ECS/Aurora inside), an account boundary even for one account, a title on top, protocol labels, a flow color code (blue request, green internal, red error, orange monitoring), and dashed return traffic. A competent diagram without it often drops the account box, colors flows arbitrarily, or leaves the logging/DLQ flows out.

floor_checks.text: diagrams/receipts.drawio parses as XML with an mxGraphModel root, at least 10 cells, all ids unique
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as E,sys,collections;r=E.parse("diagrams/receipts.drawio").getroot();r=r if r.tag=="mxGraphModel" else r.find(".//mxGraphModel");ids=[c.get("id") for c in r.iter("mxCell")];sys.exit(0 if r is not None and len(ids)==len(set(ids)) and len(ids)>=10 else 1)'

floor_checks.text: Service scope placement: CloudFront and S3 icons are outside the VPC box; Fargate/ECS and Aurora/RDS icons are inside it
floor_checks.check:
python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as E,re,sys
r=E.parse("diagrams/receipts.drawio").getroot()
r=r if r.tag=="mxGraphModel" else r.find(".//mxGraphModel")
cs={c.get("id"):c for c in r.iter("mxCell")}
def g(c):
  m=c.find("mxGeometry");x=float(m.get("x",0));y=float(m.get("y",0));w=float(m.get("width",0));h=float(m.get("height",0));p=cs.get(c.get("parent"))
  while p is not None and p.get("vertex")=="1":
    pm=p.find("mxGeometry");x+=float(pm.get("x",0));y+=float(pm.get("y",0));p=cs.get(p.get("parent"))
  return x,y,w,h
V=[c for c in cs.values() if c.get("vertex")=="1" and c.find("mxGeometry") is not None]
vp=[c for c in V if ("vpc" in (c.get("value") or "").lower() or "group_vpc" in (c.get("style") or "")) and "resIcon" not in (c.get("style") or "")]
vb=max((g(c) for c in vp),key=lambda b:b[2]*b[3])
def ins(c):
  x,y,w,h=g(c);cx,cy=x+w/2,y+h/2;return vb[0]<=cx<=vb[0]+vb[2] and vb[1]<=cy<=vb[1]+vb[3]
def ic(pat): return [c for c in V if re.search(r"mxgraph\.aws4\.("+pat+r")\b",c.get("style") or "")]
out=ic("cloudfront|s3|simple_storage_service");inn=ic("fargate|ecs|elastic_container_service|aurora|rds")
sys.exit(0 if out and inn and not any(ins(c) for c in out) and all(ins(c) for c in inn) else 1)'

rubric.criterion: Service coverage and scope placement against system-design.md (CloudFront, WAF, S3 x2, API Gateway, Cognito, Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS + DLQ, Fargate, Aurora, VPC gateway endpoint, CloudWatch, SNS)
rubric.pass: All listed services present; S3/CloudFront/WAF inside account but outside VPC; Lambda/DynamoDB/SQS/API GW outside VPC; Fargate in private and Aurora in isolated subnet inside VPC; gateway endpoint drawn on the VPC
rubric.partial: Placement correct but 1-3 services missing (typically DLQ, endpoint, CloudWatch/SNS) or subnets not distinguished
rubric.fail: A VPC-scoped/global placement error (e.g. Lambda or S3 inside the VPC) or 4+ services missing

rubric.criterion: Follows the skill's diagram conventions: title cell on top, labeled AWS account boundary and region boundary, VPC boundary, official mxgraph.aws4 icons
rubric.pass: Title above all containers naming the system and purpose, account (receipts-prod / 111122223333) and us-east-1 region containers, aws4 icons on every service
rubric.partial: One of title / account / region boundary missing, or a few services drawn as plain boxes
rubric.fail: Two or more of title, account boundary, region boundary missing, or mostly non-AWS shapes

rubric.criterion: Data flow edges: directional, labeled with protocol or data type, colored by flow type, dashed for return/intermittent traffic
rubric.pass: Every edge has an arrowhead and a label (HTTPS, SQS poll, PostgreSQL/5432, etc.); request, internal, monitoring and DLQ/alert flows use distinct colors; responses or polling shown dashed
rubric.partial: Edges directional and labeled but color coding absent or inconsistent, or no dashed return/intermittent edge
rubric.fail: Unlabeled or non-directional edges, or major flows (Lambda->SQS->Fargate->Aurora) missing

rubric.criterion: Security review usefulness: trust boundaries and auth points visible
rubric.pass: Internet/edge boundary distinguishable from the account interior; WAF shown on CloudFront and Cognito authorizing API Gateway; assumptions note lists the judgment calls made
rubric.partial: Boundaries present but auth points (WAF, Cognito) not tied to the flows they protect, or no assumptions note
rubric.fail: No way to tell where untrusted traffic enters, and no assumptions listed

rubric.pass: No services, accounts, regions or ports the doc does not support beyond what the assumptions note declares
rubric.partial: One undeclared invented component (e.g. NAT gateway, second region) that does not distort the design
rubric.fail: Several invented components or a contradiction with the doc (e.g. Lambda in the VPC, multi-account)

prompts.prompt: Security review wants a draw.io diagram of our multi-account layout to mark trust boundaries. Production account 111122223333: ALB in public subnets, ECS Fargate service in private subnets, RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ in isolated subnets, all in one VPC in us-east-1. Shared services account 444455556666: Transit Gateway and Route 53 Resolver; the production VPC attaches to the Transit Gateway and forwards DNS to the Resolver. Log archive account 777788889999: an S3 bucket receiving CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs from production. Write uncompressed XML to diagrams/multi-account.drawio. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in a text note in the diagram, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's multi-account template, title-on-top rule, flow color code (orange for logging, blue for user requests) and its emphasis on trust boundaries and AZ separation push toward a diagram where cross-account flows are visually distinct. Without it, a model tends to draw three boxes with uniformly styled, sometimes unlabeled arrows and no AZ split for Multi-AZ RDS.

floor_checks.text: File parses, ids unique, at least 10 cells
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as E,sys,collections;r=E.parse("diagrams/multi-account.drawio").getroot();r=r if r.tag=="mxGraphModel" else r.find(".//mxGraphModel");ids=[c.get("id") for c in r.iter("mxCell")];sys.exit(0 if r is not None and len(ids)==len(set(ids)) and len(ids)>=10 else 1)'

floor_checks.text: All three accounts appear as labeled containers

rubric.criterion: Correct containment: each account a labeled container; one VPC in us-east-1 in production with public/private/isolated subnet tiers; ALB in public, Fargate in private, RDS in isolated; S3 log bucket in the log-archive account outside any VPC
rubric.pass: All containment correct, subnet tiers labeled, RDS primary/standby shown across two AZs
rubric.partial: Containment correct but subnet tiers or AZ split missing
rubric.fail: A service in the wrong account or scope (e.g. S3 bucket inside the prod VPC, TGW in production)

rubric.criterion: Cross-account flows follow the skill's flow conventions
rubric.pass: CloudTrail and Flow Logs edges to the log bucket labeled and colored as logging (orange), TGW attachment and DNS forwarding edges labeled, user request path blue, all directional
rubric.partial: Flows present and labeled but not visually distinguished by type, or one cross-account flow missing

rubric.criterion: Diagram framing: title above all containers stating system and purpose; region boundary shown
rubric.pass: Title on top mentions the multi-account / trust-boundary purpose; us-east-1 region boundary present
rubric.partial: Title present but generic or not on top, or region boundary missing
rubric.fail: No title and no region boundary

rubric.criterion: Trust boundaries are legible for a security reviewer
rubric.pass: Internet ingress to the ALB, each account boundary, and the isolated data tier are visually marked as distinct trust zones; assumptions note explains choices (e.g. CloudTrail as org trail, Flow Logs delivered direct to S3)
rubric.partial: Account boundaries clear but internet ingress or data tier not marked, or no assumptions
rubric.fail: No trust-zone distinction beyond plain boxes

rubric.pass: Adds nothing beyond what the request implies, or declares additions (e.g. NAT, IGW) as assumptions

prompts.prompt: diagrams/legacy.drawio was drawn by hand and Design Inspector rejects it for threat modeling. Review it against AWS architecture diagram conventions and write the findings to diagram-review.md, ordered by severity CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION, each with the cell id it concerns and the fix. Then write a corrected version to diagrams/legacy-fixed.drawio that keeps the same three services. Use system-design.md for context. Do not ask me questions; state assumptions in the review file and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate makes wrong scope placement and missing flow direction CRITICAL, and missing boundaries and missing labels IMPORTANT. Without it a reviewer typically finds the same problems but grades them ad hoc (often treating non-directional edges as cosmetic) and may not notice that the S3 cell is only geometrically, not structurally, inside the VPC.

floor_checks.text: Review flags the S3 bucket placed inside the VPC as a scope error, under CRITICAL
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;t=open("diagram-review.md").read();c=t.upper().find("CRITICAL");i=t.upper().find("IMPORTANT");s=t[c:i if i>c else None];sys.exit(0 if c>=0 and re.search("s3|receipts-images",s,re.I) and re.search("vpc|scope",s,re.I) else 1)'
